applicabilityBasis.summary: FUSD is marketed for payments/settlement at a stable USD 1 price and distributes income by balance rebasing. The public mint/redemption policy provides equivalent USDT after fees, while GENIUS section 2(22)(A)(ii)(I) requires an issuer obligation to redeem a fixed amount of monetary value and expressly does not count a digital asset denominated in such value. No definitive public USD cash/deposit redemption obligation or fund-share/security entitlement was located. Applicability therefore remains unclear on the redemption-right evidence, not because yield or T-bill/MMF backing automatically excludes it.

genius.notes: Finchain Holdings Bermuda Limited is the issuer named in the current product structuring disclosure; Finchain Holdings (Cayman) Limited is its parent and the generic website contracting entity, not a replacement token issuer. BMA licensing remains an issuer claim: the complete official regulated-entities HTML was independently retrieved (HTTP 200; 1,780 table rows), with no Finchain-named entry located; this bounded name check is not a regulator determination that the company lacks a licence. The dedicated BMA browser attempt failed. Public issuer pages disclose reserves and USDT redemption, not a GENIUS-compliant cash-redemption certification. No independent monthly token attestation was verified: the linked DocSend native fetch denied bot access and the dedicated browser exposed no report text, so no monthly-attestation boolean is asserted. Yield/rebasing and reserve composition alone neither establish securities exclusion nor PPSI approval. The U.S. offer/sale transition is not yet a present prohibition; no registered foreign exception is asserted.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public source naming Finchain Holdings Bermuda Limited/FUSD as a U.S. GENIUS permitted issuer, state-qualified issuer, official pending applicant or registered comparable foreign issuer was located in this dated, bounded independent review. Exact-name regulator-domain searches likewise returned no token-specific public enforcement result. Opened federal materials describe proposals or transition procedures, not issuer approval; the OCC pending digital-assets bank-applicant table is not an exhaustive PPSI register. Foreign status remains unknown. The issuer-asserted Bermuda licence was not independently matched in the complete BMA HTML register, and even a confirmed Bermuda licence would not establish a U.S. permission.
